doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Leaving Baton Rouge for Opelousas and the Louisiana Ramblers
summary: He took a band to a Catholic convention in Opelousas and stayed with a family band, the Louisiana Ramblers, playing only clarinet.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: The Toothjohnker? Toothjohnker. Well, I left, uh, Baton Rouge and went to work, uh, my brother and I got a little job playing a, uh, kind of a Catholic convention in a little town named Opelousa, Louisiana, and we took a band over there, and I went to work with a, a family band. I stayed, uh, a fellow named, uh, Martell's Officer, called Louisiana Ramblers.
They offered me this job, and, uh, I stayed and worked with them.
At this time, you were playing only clarinet, huh? That's right.
